Class Arguments

java.lang.Object
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.Arguments
public class Arguments extends Object
A wrapper for the string arguments passed to a Java program's main method that provides ways to check which arguments exist, what their values are, and which have been used.

The Argument class provides a way to get and parse specific arguments and to document their purpose.

Author:
Stephen G. Ware

    • contains

      public boolean contains(String key)
      Returns true if the given key appears in this collection of arguments. A key is an argument that begins with a dash. The string given to this method may include the dash or not. For example, if this method is called with the string "example", it will return true if if the string "-example" appear in this collection of arguments. The string given to this method can be either "example" or "-example". This method marks the key as used if it is found.
      Parameters:
      key - the key to search for
      Returns:
      true if these arguments contains the given key

    • get

      public String get(String key)
      Returns the value that appears after a key, or null if the key or value does not exist. A key is an argument that begins with a dash, and a value must not begin with a dash. The string given to this method may include the dash or not. For example, if this collection of arguments contains "-key val", then this method will return "val" when called with the string "key" or "-key". This method marks the key and value as used if they are found.
      Parameters:
      key - the key to search for
      Returns:
      the value immediately after the key, if the key was found an has a value after it, or null if the key or value does not exist

    • require

      public String require(String key)
      Returns the value that appears after a key, or throws an exception if the key or value does not exist. A key is an argument that begins with a dash, and a value must not begin with a dash. The string given to this method may include the dash or not. For example, if this collection of arguments contains "-key val", then this method will return "val" when called with the string "key" or "-key". This method marks the key and value as used if they are found.
      Parameters:
      key - the key to search for
      Returns:
      the value immediately after the key
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the key was not found or if there was no value after it
